name: Takeoff bulk operations and import
summary: Working with many takeoff assets at once: a creation session that saves or discards a batch, count categories drawn as symbols, bulk and filter-based deletion, linking progress assets to takeoff assets, the takeoff change history, and importing takeoff from a spreadsheet or from Arth output.

requirements.title: A takeoff creation session saves or discards its whole batch
requirements.statement: A user picks a category and stage settings once, then draws any number of takeoff assets. A running total for each stage across the structure updates as they draw. Saving creates every asset in the session in one request; leaving with unsaved assets asks for confirmation and then discards them.
requirements.rationale: Matches the bulk creation mode in the takeoff-management PRD (FR-004..FR-006). The PRD's tooltip for changing the configuration after drawing was not traced in code.

requirements.title: Count categories turn drawn lines and polygons into one symbol
requirements.statement: When every stage of a category is measured by count and the category has a fixed shape, a line or polygon drawn as takeoff is saved as a single symbol. A polygon becomes a symbol at its centre; a line becomes a symbol at the point halfway along its length.
requirements.rationale: Supports count-based scopes such as electrical devices (electrical PRD goal of partial progress by counts).

requirements.title: Deleting takeoff linked to progress unlinks the progress assets
requirements.statement: Deleting a takeoff asset, one at a time, in bulk or by filter, removes it and silently removes the link from any progress asset that pointed to it. The PRD says such a deletion should be blocked and the user told about the dependency.

dispute.summary: takeoff-management.md EC-007 says deleting a takeoff asset linked to progress assets must be prevented. The code deletes it and pulls the takeoff ID from linked progress assets without warning.

requirements.title: Bulk takeoff deletion is all or nothing, and filter deletes respect review state
requirements.statement: Deleting selected takeoff assets fails without deleting anything if any selected asset no longer exists. Deleting by structure and categories reaches only active takeoff for customers; for support users it also reaches takeoff that is in review or inactive. The same scope applies to filter-based updates.
requirements.rationale: Covers the PRD's bulk delete for end users and for the Arth review team (FR-007, FR-008, EC-005).

requirements.title: Progress assets are linked to the takeoff assets they measure
requirements.statement: Progress assets can be linked to, and unlinked from, one or more takeoff assets in one action. Every link is recorded in the progress audit log with the user. Linking fails if any named takeoff asset does not exist.
requirements.rationale: This is how progress is marked per capture against a takeoff asset, as the electrical PRD asks (FR-002) and as the takeoff PRD's "create progress assets from takeoff assets" story describes (US-008, FR-011).

requirements.title: Takeoff changes are recorded with who made them and when
requirements.statement: Creating and deleting takeoff assets writes a progress audit entry with the user, the category and the effective date. The PRD also asks for a "View history" option beside "Edit takeoff" on the progress overview that shows these changes with user details and timestamps.
requirements.rationale: The audit entries exist in code; a history view reading them for takeoff was not found. The PRD rules out rolling back to earlier takeoff from the history panel.

requirements.title: Import takeoff quantities from a spreadsheet
requirements.statement: A user with upload rights downloads a template, fills it and uploads csv, xlsx or xls up to 50 MB. The file is validated with clear errors; empty or unsupported files are rejected. A partial file changes only the structures it names, and rows for structures that don't exist are ignored. Every upload is kept in an upload history.
requirements.rationale: PRD only for the spreadsheet route. Overwrite default, unit enforcement and auto-creating categories are open (DEC-079).
